climate_pressure: Positive temperature anomalies and/or negative precipitation anomalies.
documented_impact: Changes in maize production and household food-security status.
fcv_mediator: Household food insecurity and livelihood stress.
possible_consequence: Higher subsequent incidence of several ACLED conflict-event categories, conditional on the study model.
uncertainty: Structural-equation mediation is compatible with the pathway but does not establish event-level climate causality. (Frontiers) Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
compact_statement: Climate anomalies may contribute to conflict risk through crop and food-security effects, but the observed relationship is mediated and non-deterministic.

climate_pressure: Drought, inadequate rain, late or variable rainy seasons.
documented_impact: Changes in pasture/water availability and livestock movement.
fcv_mediator: Rules governing access to land, water and seasonal routes; interaction among farmers and pastoral groups.
possible_consequence: Local disputes or violence may become more likely where mobility intersects poorly governed or contested access.
geographies: Inner Niger Delta and pastoral corridors
uncertainty: Mobility is itself an adaptation strategy and must not be characterized as inherently destabilizing. (SIPRI) Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
compact_statement: Rainfall stress can alter pastoral mobility, but whether this becomes conflict depends heavily on institutions and access governance.

documented_impact: Crop losses, erosion and potential infrastructure damage; FAO specifically reported 2024 flood-related crop losses.
fcv_mediator: Food prices, market access, household asset depletion and uneven assistance.
possible_consequence: Higher vulnerability, displacement or local grievances may result where recovery and markets are weak.
uncertainty: No retained source directly demonstrates that specific Mali floods caused subsequent violence. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
compact_statement: Flood losses can deepen food and livelihood stress, but an FCV consequence requires additional social and institutional mediators. (World Bank)

climate_pressure: Drought, heat and rainfall-related livelihood stress.
documented_impact: Reduced or more uncertain natural-resource-based livelihood options.
fcv_mediator: Poverty, unemployment, absence of alternatives, grievances and armed-group economic incentives.
possible_consequence: Recruitment vulnerability may increase for some individuals.
geographies: Principally northern and central Mali in the retained qualitative evidence
uncertainty: SIPRI explicitly describes recruitment as complex and the study as a plausibility probe. (SIPRI) Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
compact_statement: Climate stress may narrow livelihoods and thereby enlarge recruitment opportunities, but it is one contributor among many.

climate_pressure: Drought/rainfall variability remains the environmental stressor to which livelihood systems need to adapt.
documented_impact: Conflict disrupted irrigation and livestock markets and pushed some herds southward.
fcv_mediator: Insecurity, market closure and constrained movement.
possible_consequence: Households may lose access to otherwise effective drought-coping options and face greater resource pressure elsewhere.
uncertainty: Qualitative evidence documents coping strategies and conflict disruption, but does not estimate the incremental loss of climate-adaptation performance. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
compact_statement: Conflict can disable livelihood strategies that would otherwise help households adapt to climatic variability. (SIPRI)

climate_pressure: Increasing heat, variable rainfall, drought/flood exposure.
documented_impact: Growing pressure on natural-resource management and demand for coordinated adaptation.
fcv_mediator: Weak institutional coordination, limited budgets, unequal access and weak local governance.
possible_consequence: Adaptation gaps and perceived unfairness may aggravate grievances or disputes.
geographies: with greater constraints in conflict-prone localities
uncertainty: Institutional weakness is independently consequential and should not be relabelled as a climate effect. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
compact_statement: Climate pressures place additional demands on already constrained institutions; weak or unequal responses can in turn worsen both vulnerability and grievance risk. (World Bank)

documented_impact: Need for mobility, livelihood adjustment and collective natural-resource management.
fcv_mediator: Local legitimacy, dispute resolution, collective decision-making and grievance handling.
possible_consequence: Locally legitimate institutions may support coping and reduce escalation risk, but the planned committee mechanism and peace effects are not observed outcomes.
geographies: specific evidence should not be generalized to all Mali
alternative_explanations: Some local institutions can also reproduce exclusion or unequal access
uncertainty: Strong independent evidence on peace outcomes from climate/resource institutions remains limited. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
compact_statement: Locally legitimate coping and resource-governance institutions are plausible peace-supporting capacities, but their distributional and conflict effects require evaluation.

climate_pressure: Dry-season water scarcity described by Dembala residents.
documented_impact: Pump/well failures restricted drinking water and vegetable-growing access.
fcv_mediator: Competition at scarce shared water points amid livelihood pressure.
possible_consequence: Residents reported fights over water; the story does not establish violence incidence or a climate-attributable effect.
alternative_explanations: Pump maintenance, local water governance and livelihood conditions also shape scarcity and disputes.
uncertainty: Historical resident testimony in a 2025 implementer story; village district not verified; not a representative causal study. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Reported water-point rehabilitation restored access, but conflict reduction was not independently evaluated.
compact_statement: Dembala residents linked dry-season water-point failures with livelihood constraints and disputes; rehabilitation is a reported capacity response.
